from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.",
            "They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.",
            "Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.",
            "This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.",
            "Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Camera at B2
        camera_body = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.4, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1)
        camera_lens = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.05)
        camera = VGroup(camera_body, camera_lens)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, "B2")
        
        # Cube (2D representation) at B4
        cube_obj = Square(side_length=0.6, color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_obj, "B4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(camera), FadeIn(cube_obj))
        
        # Flash animation
        flash = Flash(self.grid["B4"], color=WHITE, line_length=0.2, num_lines=12)
        self.play(flash)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#B0C4DE"))
        
        # 2D result at B6
        photo_rect = Square(side_length=0.6, color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(photo_rect, "B6")
        label_2d = Text("2D Intensity Map", font_size=18, color="#B0C4DE")
        label_2d.next_to(photo_rect, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        conn_arrow = Arrow(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["B6"], buff=0.4, color="#B0C4DE")
        
        self.play(Create(conn_arrow), FadeIn(photo_rect), Write(label_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Laser setup
        laser_box = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=0.3, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(laser_box, "D1")
        
        bs_mirror = Square(side_length=0.4, color=WHITE).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(bs_mirror, "D3")
        
        laser_beam_1 = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(laser_box), FadeIn(bs_mirror))
        self.play(Create(laser_beam_1))
        
        # Split beams
        ref_beam = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["F3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=3)
        obj_beam = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D5"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(Create(ref_beam), Create(obj_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#A9A9A9"))
        
        # Plate and wavefronts
        plate_rect = Rectangle(width=0.15, height=1.2, color="#A9A9A9", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(plate_rect, "F3")
        
        cube_3d_ref = Cube(side_length=0.7, stroke_color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_3d_ref, "D5")
        
        scattered_beam = Line(self.grid["D5"], self.grid["F3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Simple wavefront arcs
        wavefronts = VGroup(*[
            Arc(radius=0.2+i*0.2, start_angle=-60*DEGREES, angle=120*DEGREES, color="#A9A9A9")
            for i in range(3)
        ])
        wavefronts.move_to(self.grid["D5"])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cube_3d_ref), FadeIn(plate_rect))
        self.play(Create(scattered_beam))
        self.play(wavefronts.animate.shift(RIGHT*1.5 + DOWN*1.5).set_opacity(0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Final 3D hologram emerges in the bottom right area
        hologram = Cube(side_length=1.4, stroke_color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(hologram, "D4", "F6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(hologram))
        
        # Use an updater for continuous rotation to simulate changing perspective
        hologram.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 0.8, axis=UP))
        hologram.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 0.3, axis=RIGHT))
        
        self.wait(5)
        hologram.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # --- Data Setup ---
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Language of Waves"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_WAVE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_PEAK = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_TROUGH = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_INTERFERENCE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_DIM = "#666666"

        # Wave boundary points using grid positions C1 to C6
        start_pt = self.grid["C1"]
        end_pt = self.grid["C6"]
        start_x = float(start_pt[0])
        end_x = float(end_pt[0])
        wave_y = float(start_pt[1])
        wave_width = end_x - start_x

        # Trackers for animation
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0.0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(0.7)
        phase_tracker2 = ValueTracker(np.pi) # Second wave offset for initial interference

        def get_wave_points(phase, amp):
            res = 80
            pts = []
            for i in range(res + 1):
                pct = float(i) / res
                curr_x = start_x + pct * wave_width
                # Wave equation: y = baseline + amp * sin(2*pi*cycles*pct - phase)
                # 2 cycles across the width
                curr_y = wave_y + float(amp) * np.sin(4.0 * np.pi * pct - float(phase))
                pts.append([curr_x, curr_y, 0.0])
            return pts

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_WAVE), run_time=0.5)
        
        wave1 = VMobject(color=COLOR_WAVE)
        wave1.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(0.0, 0.7))
        wave1.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(wave1)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        peak_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_PEAK, radius=0.1)
        trough_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_TROUGH, radius=0.1)

        def update_peak(d):
            p = float(phase_tracker.get_value())
            amp = float(amp_tracker.get_value())
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = 1 => 4*pi*pct - p = pi/2 => pct = (pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (np.pi / 2.0 + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5 # Period is 0.5 in pct units
            d.move_to([start_x + pct * wave_width, wave_y + amp, 0.0])

        def update_trough(d):
            p = float(phase_tracker.get_value())
            amp = float(amp_tracker.get_value())
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = -1 => 4*pi*pct - p = 3*pi/2 => pct = (3*pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (1.5 * np.pi + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5
            d.move_to([start_x + pct * wave_width, wave_y - amp, 0.0])

        peak_dot.add_updater(update_peak)
        trough_dot.add_updater(update_trough)
        
        self.add(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.remove(peak_dot, trough_dot)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Introduce secondary wave (initially out of phase)
        wave2 = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        wave2.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), 0.7))
        wave2.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), 0.7)
        ))
        
        self.add(wave2)
        self.wait(1.0)

        # Phase alignment (Transition to constructive interference)
        self.play(
            phase_tracker2.animate.set_value(phase_tracker.get_value()),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Merge: increase amplitude of first wave and fade out the second
        # Note: both are driven by updaters, so we just animate the tracker
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wave2),
            amp_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4),
            wave1.animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        
        # Final oscillation of the constructive interference result
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(6.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint", [
            "A laser beam is split into two separate paths.",
            "The object beam reflects off the subject being recorded.",
            "The reference beam travels directly to the holographic film.",
            "These beams collide, creating a complex interference pattern.",
            "This microscopic pattern encodes the object's 3D information."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        laser_color = "#FF0000"
        teapot_color = "#B0C4DE"
        fringe_color = "#E6E6FA"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A red laser #FF0000 splits into two beams at a splitter.
        source = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(source, "B1")
        source_label = Text("Laser", font_size=16).next_to(source, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        splitter = Rectangle(height=0.6, width=0.1, color=WHITE).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(splitter, "B2")
        splitter_label = Text("Splitter", font_size=14).next_to(splitter, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        initial_beam = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["B2"], color=laser_color)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(source), FadeIn(source_label), FadeIn(splitter), FadeIn(splitter_label))
        self.play(Create(initial_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # One beam reflects off a teapot #B0C4DE onto a plate.
        teapot_body = Ellipse(width=0.6, height=0.4, color=teapot_color, fill_opacity=0.6)
        teapot_handle = Arc(radius=0.15, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=PI, color=teapot_color).shift(RIGHT*0.3)
        teapot_spout = Line(LEFT*0.3, LEFT*0.5 + UP*0.2, color=teapot_color)
        teapot = VGroup(teapot_body, teapot_handle, teapot_spout)
        self.place_at_grid(teapot, "B5")
        teapot_label = Text("Teapot", font_size=16, color=teapot_color).next_to(teapot, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        plate = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=0.2, color=GREY_A, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(plate, "E6")
        plate_label = Text("Film", font_size=16).next_to(plate, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        object_beam_part1 = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B5"], color=laser_color)
        object_beam_part2 = Line(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["E6"], color=laser_color)
        obj_label = Text("Object Beam", font_size=12, color=laser_color).next_to(object_beam_part1, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(teapot), FadeIn(teapot_label), FadeIn(plate), FadeIn(plate_label))
        self.play(Create(object_beam_part1), FadeIn(obj_label))
        self.play(Create(object_beam_part2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A second beam travels directly to the plate as a reference.
        mirror = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.05, color=WHITE).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(mirror, "E2")
        mirror_label = Text("Mirror", font_size=14).next_to(mirror, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        ref_beam_part1 = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["E2"], color=laser_color)
        ref_beam_part2 = Line(self.grid["E2"], self.grid["E6"], color=laser_color)
        ref_label = Text("Reference Beam", font_size=12, color=laser_color).next_to(ref_beam_part2, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(mirror), FadeIn(mirror_label))
        self.play(Create(ref_beam_part1))
        self.play(Create(ref_beam_part2), FadeIn(ref_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Both beams meet, forming an interference pattern #E6E6FA on the plate.
        fringes = VGroup(*[
            Line(UP*0.7, DOWN*0.7, color=fringe_color, stroke_width=0.8).shift(RIGHT * x)
            for x in np.linspace(-0.06, 0.06, 12)
        ])
        fringes.move_to(plate.get_center())
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(fringes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Zoom into the plate showing microscopic details of the pattern.
        zoom_pattern = VGroup()
        for i in range(25):
            x_off = -2.5 + i * 0.2
            pts = [np.array([x_off + 0.1 * np.sin(y * 3 + i), y, 0]) for y in np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 30)]
            line = VMobject(color=fringe_color, stroke_width=1.5)
            line.set_points_as_corners(pts)
            zoom_pattern.add(line)
        
        self.place_in_area(zoom_pattern, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        setup_group = VGroup(source, source_label, splitter, splitter_label, initial_beam, 
                            teapot, teapot_label, plate, plate_label, object_beam_part1, object_beam_part2,
                            obj_label, mirror, mirror_label, ref_beam_part1, ref_beam_part2, ref_label, fringes)
        
        self.play(
            setup_group.animate.set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(zoom_pattern)
        )
        self.wait(3)
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light"
        lines = [
            "Diffraction bends light as it passes through tiny openings.",
            "Holographic patterns act as microscopic gratings for light waves.",
            "This bending recreates the original path of the light."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Parallel white wave fronts #FFFFFF approach a narrow vertical slit.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Slit setup: A barrier with a small gap
        slit_top = Line(UP*1.5, UP*0.15, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        slit_bottom = Line(DOWN*0.15, DOWN*1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        slit_barrier = VGroup(slit_top, slit_bottom)
        self.place_at_grid(slit_barrier, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Incoming wave fronts
        wave_fronts = VGroup(*[
            Line(UP*1.2, DOWN*1.2, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
            for _ in range(4)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_fronts, "C1", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Animate waves approaching the slit
        self.add(slit_barrier, wave_fronts)
        self.play(
            wave_fronts.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.8),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # As the waves pass through, they transform into orange circular arcs #FFA500 spreading outward.
        # Holographic patterns act as microscopic gratings for light waves.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFA500")
        )
        
        # Create orange circular arcs centered at the slit
        slit_center = self.grid["C3"]
        arcs = VGroup(*[
            Arc(
                radius=r, 
                start_angle=-PI/3, 
                angle=2*PI/3, 
                arc_center=slit_center, 
                color="#FFA500",
                stroke_width=3
            ) for r in [0.2, 0.6, 1.0, 1.4]
        ])
        
        # Transition from straight waves to arcs
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wave_fronts),
            Create(arcs),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Introduce multiple slits (grating) and the grating equation
        grating = VGroup()
        for i in range(-6, 7):
            grating.add(Line(LEFT*0.15, RIGHT*0.15, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).shift(UP*i*0.25))
        grating.rotate(PI/2)
        self.place_at_grid(grating, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        equation = MathTex("d \\sin(\\theta) = m\\lambda", color="#FFA500", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(slit_barrier),
            FadeIn(grating),
            Write(equation),
            arcs.animate.scale(1.3).shift(RIGHT * 0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Multiple slits appear, creating a pattern of bright and dark spots #FF6347 on a distant screen.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347")
        )
        
        # Ddistant screen at column 6
        screen = Line(UP*2.5, DOWN*2.5, color=GREY_B, stroke_width=6)
        self.place_at_grid(screen, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Interference pattern: Bright spots (Central maximum is brightest)
        spots = VGroup()
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            # Diminishing intensity for higher order spots
            opacity = 1.0 if i == 0 else (0.7 if abs(i) == 1 else (0.4 if abs(i) == 2 else 0.2))
            dot = Dot(color="#FF6347", radius=0.18).set_opacity(opacity)
            spots.add(dot.shift(UP * i * 0.75))
        self.place_at_grid(spots, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Light rays from grating to spots to visualize the "bending"
        grating_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        rays = VGroup(*[
            Line(grating_pos, spot.get_center(), color="#FF6347", stroke_width=1).set_opacity(0.3)
            for spot in spots
        ])
        
        self.play(
            Create(screen),
            LaggedStart(*[Create(r) for r in rays], lag_ratio=0.1),
            FadeIn(spots, shift=RIGHT*0.2),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(3)
from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Reconstruction: Bringing the Ghost to Life", [
            "To see the image, we use the reference beam.",
            "Illuminating the hologram causes the light to diffract.",
            "The diffracted light waves perfectly mimic the original object.",
            "We see a three-dimensional \"ghost\" of the recorded object.",
            "The original wavefront is recreated, restoring depth and perspective."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        LASER_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        RAY_COLOR = "#87CEEB"
        GHOST_COLOR = "#F0FFF0"

        # Plate
        plate = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=4, color=PLATE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(plate, "B2", "E2")
        
        # Laser Beam
        laser_source = Dot(color=LASER_COLOR).move_to(self.grid["C1"])

        self.play(Create(plate), FadeIn(laser_source))
        self.play(Create(laser_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Illuminating the hologram causes the light to diffract.
        # Blue light rays #87CEEB diffract and bend through the plate.
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RAY_COLOR)
        
        diffracted_rays = VGroup(*[
            Line(self.grid["C2"], self.grid[f"{row}5"], color=RAY_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
            for row in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(diffracted_rays))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The diffracted light waves perfectly mimic the original object.
        # The light rays reconstruct the original object's complex wavefront.
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RAY_COLOR)
        
        # Wavefront arcs
        wavefronts = VGroup(*[
            Arc(radius=r, start_angle=-PI/3, angle=2*PI/3, color=RAY_COLOR, stroke_opacity=1-r/4)
            .move_to(self.grid["C2"] + RIGHT * r)
            for r in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0]
        ])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(wavefronts, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # We see a three-dimensional "ghost" of the recorded object.
        # A shimmering virtual teapot #F0FFF0 appears in mid-air.
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GHOST_COLOR)
        
        # Teapot representation (simple 2D)
        teapot_body = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GHOST_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4)
        teapot_handle = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=PI/2, angle=PI, color=GHOST_COLOR)
        teapot_handle.next_to(teapot_body, LEFT, buff=-0.1)
        teapot_spout = Triangle(color=GHOST_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4).scale(0.2)
        teapot_spout.rotate(-PI/2).next_to(teapot_body, RIGHT, buff=-0.1)
        teapot = VGroup(teapot_body, teapot_handle, teapot_spout)
        self.place_in_area(teapot, "C4", "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Shimmer effect using a ValueTracker and updater
        shimmer_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        teapot.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.set_opacity(0.6 + 0.3 * np.sin(shimmer_tracker.get_value() * 5)))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(teapot))
        self.play(shimmer_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The original wavefront is recreated, restoring depth and perspective.
        # The teapot #F0FFF0 rotates, revealing its three-dimensional structure.
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GHOST_COLOR)
        
        # Rotate around UP axis to simulate depth in a 2D scene
        self.play(Rotate(teapot, angle=TAU, axis=UP, run_time=3))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR"
        lines = [
            "Tiny diffraction gratings provide security on credit cards.",
            "Head-up displays use these principles to project transparent data.",
            "Holography brings 3D visuals to modern engineering and art."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a silver credit card
        card = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=2.0, width=3.2, 
                               fill_opacity=1, fill_color="#C0C0C0", stroke_color=WHITE)
        
        # Simple bird shape for hologram
        bird_body = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color="#FF0000")
        wing_l = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=0.5*PI, angle=PI, color="#FF0000").rotate(0.5*PI)
        wing_r = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=0.5*PI, angle=PI, color="#FF0000").rotate(-0.5*PI)
        wing_l.shift(LEFT*0.1)
        wing_r.shift(RIGHT*0.1)
        bird = VGroup(bird_body, wing_l, wing_r).scale(0.5)
        
        # Position bird on the card
        bird.move_to(card.get_center())
        card_group = VGroup(card, bird)
        self.place_in_area(card_group, "A4", "C6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(card_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        hud_bg = Rectangle(height=2.0, width=3.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2)
        hud_text = Text("HEADING: 090", font_size=16, color=TEAL)
        hud_group = VGroup(hud_bg, hud_text)
        self.place_in_area(hud_group, "D4", "F6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(hud_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Visual for holography
        holo_shape = Star(color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.7).scale(1.2)
        self.place_in_area(holo_shape, "B4", "E6")
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(card_group, holo_shape),
            FadeOut(hud_group)
        )
        self.play(Rotate(holo_shape, angle=TAU, run_time=2))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Principles of Holography and Diffraction: Capturing the Ghost of Light
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Physics/Engineering Students or Advanced High School Students

sections.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
sections.content: Introduction to the fundamental difference between traditional photography and holography. Explain that while photos record only brightness (intensity), holograms record the 'depth' and 'shape' of light waves.
sections.example: An animated cat tries to pounce on a 2D photo of a mouse and fails to see depth, then encounters a 3D holographic mouse that it can walk around, seeing different angles as it moves.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Waves
sections.content: Review of wave properties: Amplitude (brightness) and Phase (position in the wave cycle). Introduce Constructive and Destructive Interference as the 'building blocks' of holographic patterns.
sections.example: Visualizing two pebbles dropped in a pond. Where the ripples meet and get taller is 'constructive' interference; where they cancel out is 'destructive'. Animation shows the peaks and troughs aligning.

sections.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
sections.content: Explain the setup of a laser beam split into two: The 'Object Beam' (hits the subject) and the 'Reference Beam' (stays pure). Their collision creates an 'Interference Pattern' on the film.
sections.example: A laser beam hits a mirror. Half the light bounces off a 'Golden Dragon' figurine (Object Beam), while the other half hits the film directly (Reference Beam). The film looks like messy noise, not a dragon.

sections.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light
sections.content: Introducing the concept of Diffraction. When light hits the microscopic 'interference pattern' (which acts like a complex grating), it bends. Introduce the simplified Grating Equation: d sin(θ) = mλ, using graphics to show how spacing (d) affects the angle (θ).
sections.example: Animation of light passing through a picket fence. If the slats are close together, the light fan-out is wider. The 'messy noise' on the holographic plate is actually a trillion tiny 'fences' that bend light back into the shape of the original object.

sections.title: Reconstruction: Bringing the Ghost to Life
sections.content: Explain how shining the Reference Beam back through the processed hologram 'reconstructs' the wavefront of the original object through diffraction.
sections.example: The 'Golden Dragon' is gone. We shine the laser through the 'noisy' plate. Because of the diffraction math (d sin θ), the light waves exit the plate exactly as they did when they bounced off the dragon. The cat from Section 1 sees the dragon's 'ghost' floating in space.

sections.title: Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR
sections.content: Brief summary of applications. How microscopic diffraction gratings are used for security and modern head-up displays (HUDs).
sections.example: Zooming into the shimmering dove on a credit card to show the microscopic lines, then transitioning to a pilot's helmet display showing holographic flight data overlaid on the real world.

storyboard.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
lecture_lines: Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.
They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.
Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.
This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.
Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object.
animations: A camera #FFFFFF takes a picture of a cube #B0C4DE, creating a flat 2D image.
The flat image is highlighted to show captured light intensity.
A red laser #FF0000 splits, hitting both a cube and plate #A9A9A9.
A complex interference pattern appears on the plate #A9A9A9.
A green 3D cube #00FF00 emerges and rotates from the plate.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Waves
lecture_lines: Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.
Interference happens when two light waves overlap.
Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out.
animations: A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally across the black background.
The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF to show phase.
Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.

storyboard.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
lecture_lines: A laser beam is split into two separate paths.
The object beam reflects off the subject being recorded.
The reference beam travels directly to the holographic film.
These beams collide, creating a complex interference pattern.
This microscopic pattern encodes the object's 3D information.
animations: A red laser [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] #FF0000 splits into two beams at a splitter.
One beam reflects off a teapot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/teapot.svg] #B0C4DE onto a plate.
A second beam travels directly to the plate as a reference.
Both beams meet, forming an interference pattern #E6E6FA on the plate.
Zoom into the plate showing microscopic details of the pattern.

storyboard.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light
lecture_lines: Diffraction bends light as it passes through tiny openings.
Holographic patterns act as microscopic gratings for light waves.
This bending recreates the original path of the light.
animations: Parallel white wave fronts #FFFFFF approach a narrow vertical [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slit.svg] slit.
As the waves pass through, they transform into orange circular arcs #FFA500 spreading outward.

Multiple [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slit.svg] slits appear, creating a pattern of bright and dark spots #FF6347 on a distant [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/screen.svg] screen.

storyboard.title: Reconstruction: Bringing the Ghost to Life
lecture_lines: To see the image, we use the reference beam.
Illuminating the hologram causes the light to diffract.
The diffracted light waves perfectly mimic the original object.
We see a three-dimensional "ghost" of the recorded object.
The original wavefront is recreated, restoring depth and perspective.
animations: A red laser #FF0000 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] shines through a holographic plate.
Blue light rays #87CEEB diffract and bend through the plate.
The light rays reconstruct the original object's complex wavefront.
A shimmering virtual teapot #F0FFF0 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/teapot.svg] appears in mid-air.
The teapot #F0FFF0 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/teapot.svg] rotates, revealing its three-dimensional structure.

storyboard.title: Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR
lecture_lines: Tiny diffraction gratings provide security on credit cards.
Head-up displays use these principles to project transparent data.
Holography brings 3D visuals to modern engineering and art.
animations: A silver credit card #C0C0C0 is shown with a bird-shaped hologram in the corner.
The card tilts, and the bird's color shifts smoothly from red #FF0000 to blue #0000FF.
